In [[mathematics]], specifically [[category theory]], a '''doctrine''' is roughly a system of theories ("categorical analogues of fragments of [[logical theory|logical theories]] which have sufficient category-theoretic structure for their [[Model category|models]] to be described as [[functors]]"<ref name=KochReyes-1993>{{cite book |last1=Kock |first1=A. |last2=Reyes |first2=G.E. |title=Handbook of Mathematical Logic |date=1993 |volume= |pages=283–313 |doi=10.1016/S0049-237X(08)71104-2|isbn=0444863885 |url=https://www.academia.edu/50925989/HANDBOOK_OF_MATHEMATICAL_LOGIC |editor-first= Jon | editor-last = Barwise|publisher = Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.| chapter=Doctrines in Categorical Logic }}</ref>{{rp|284}}).  For example, an [[algebraic theory]], as invented by [[William Lawvere]], is an example of a doctrine.<ref name=KochReyes-1993/>{{rp|289}}
The concept of doctrines was invented by Lawvere as part of his work on algebraic theories.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lawvere |first1=F. William |editor1-last=Eckmann |editor1-first=B. |title=Ordinal sums and equational doctrines |journal=Seminar on Triples and Categorical Homology Theory |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |date=1969 |volume=80 |pages=141–155 |doi=10.1007/BFb0083085 |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/BFb0083085 |access-date=9 April 2025 |publisher=Springer |location=Berlin |isbn=978-3-540-04601-1 |language=en|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=MarquisReyes/>{{rp|12}} The name is based on a suggestion by [[Jonathan Mock Beck|Jon Beck]].<ref name=MarquisReyes>Marquis, Jean-Pierre, and Gonzalo Reyes. [https://philarchive.org/archive/MARTHO-8 "The history of categorical logic: 1963-1977."] (2004).</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lambert |first1=Michael |last2=Patterson |first2=Evan |title=Cartesian Double Theories: A Double-categorical Framework for Categorical Doctrines |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |date=May 2024 |volume=444 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2024.109630|arxiv=2310.05384 }}</ref>

A doctrine can be defined in several ways:<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=doctrine in nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/doctrine |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>
* as a 2-[[Monad (category theory)|monad]]. This was Lawvere's original approach.
* as a [[2-category]]; the idea is that each object there amounts to a "theory".<ref name="auto"/>
* As cartesian double theories, as logics, or as a class of limits.
